column4: Visit note | 2026-03-03 02:00 PM | Dr. Tanvir Ahmed, General Medicine | Patient: Fatema Rahman, 46, female. Mrs. Rahman reports a dull discomfort in her belly and notices a coated tongue. She states that these symptoms started after drinking roadside juice in Tangail. She works as a ride-share driver and lives in the local area. She denies vomiting, chest pain, or abnormal bowel habits. On examination: temperature 101.1°F, BP 112/79 mmHg, pulse 98 bpm, weight 64 kg. Abdomen is soft with mild tenderness in the right lower quadrant, and no organomegaly. Assessment: Typhoid fever. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to eat soft home-cooked food, drink boiled or bottled water only, and avoid street food. Follow-up in 7 days with a repeat blood count.
